about: Millbrook Vineyards & Winery sits on a 130-acre former dairy farm in Dutchess County, about ninety minutes north of New York City. John Dyson, a Millbrook native who served as New York’s Commissioner of Agriculture and Markets and was behind the “I Love New York” campaign, bought the bankrupt farm in 1982. Encouraged by Finger Lakes pioneer Dr. Konstantin Frank, he planted European vinifera grapes in 1983, an unusual bet for the Hudson Valley at the time, and released the first vintage in 1985.

Today the estate has about 30 acres of vines, and Millbrook also draws on other New York vineyards and on the family’s own California vineyards. Hunt Country Red is the winery’s everyday red blend, labelled New York State. Millbrook does not publish the current blend; over the years the wine has been built mostly on Merlot and Cabernet Franc. Longtime winemaker John Graziano, at Millbrook since 1984, has retired, and Ian Beaurup, who trained in California, Oregon and New Zealand, now leads the cellar.

Millbrook describes Hunt Country Red as one of its most versatile food wines: medium in weight and soft in texture, with jammy blackberry and plum on the nose and darker berry fruit on the palate. The winery suggests it with roast pork loin, beef kebabs or a grilled rustic pizza, which makes it an easy match for food from a wood-fired kitchen.
